skill.name: datacircle
skill.description: Look up people's LinkedIn profiles by URL with Datacircle, no markup, and manage the Datacircle balance and files. Use when the user gives LinkedIn profile URLs to enrich or research (a candidate, a customer, a person in their CRM), asks what their Datacircle balance is, or wants the co-op flat file.
skill.summary: Enrich supplied LinkedIn profile URLs with approved Datacircle lookups, report costs, check balances, and share file download links.
skill.author: waynehamadi

security_audit.summary: All 12 static findings are false positives: Markdown identifiers, pricing disclosures, and download guidance do not execute commands or inspect the system. The skill requires spending approval and treats tool results as untrusted data. No evidence found of malicious intent or prompt injection in SKILL.md; the external MCP implementation was not included.

finding_verdicts.reason: Backticks format the Datacircle MCP server name in Markdown. The surrounding instruction restricts tool use to user requests and contains no shell execution.
The backticks format the get_linkedin_profile tool name, not executable shell syntax. The instruction limits lookups to URLs supplied by the user.
Backticks mark provider identifiers in Markdown. The text describes provider selection for requested profile lookups and does not invoke Ruby or a shell.
The backticks format an HTTP status code and a provider name. This is prose about rate limits and returned interests, not command execution.
Backticks format response metadata keys for cost and balance reporting. No executable statement or shell command appears here.
Backticks identify the free get_balance tool and an insufficient-balance HTTP status. The text requests a balance explanation, not shell execution.
Backticks format add_funds and checkout_url as tool and response identifiers. The instruction requires an explicit funding request and returns a user-operated checkout link.
Backticks format the get_balance tool name in a payment verification instruction. It prevents unsupported funding claims and contains no executable shell syntax.
Backticks format list_files, is_unlocked, and provider file identifiers. This is documentation for listing service files, not a command execution mechanism.
Backticks format the get_download_link tool name. The instruction only shares an expiring link and explicitly prohibits fetching the large files.
The line requires provider and price disclosure before paid lookups. It neither queries system information nor instructs the assistant to inspect the host.
The line describes download link expiry and remote file sizes, not host reconnaissance. It explicitly tells the assistant not to fetch the files.

content.value_statement: Profile research can require several lookups and careful spending control. This skill guides approved Datacircle enrichment, summarizes profiles, and reports costs and balances.
actual_capabilities: Guides one profile lookup per user-supplied LinkedIn URL and summarizes returned roles, companies, history, and skills.
Uses Up2Data by default and requests renewed approval before switching to HarvestAPI or Fetchin.
Discloses provider prices before lookups and reports total costs and remaining balance for multiple profiles.
Checks balances and shares Stripe Checkout links only when the user requests funding.
Lists provider flat files and shares download links valid for one hour without fetching large datasets.
Instructs the assistant to treat profile text and file rows as data, not executable instructions.
limitations: Requires access to a configured Datacircle MCP server; this skill contains instructions, not the server implementation.
Paid lookups require sufficient balance and explicit user approval; providers may return missing profiles or rate limits.
Does not discover additional profile URLs or guarantee profile accuracy, completeness, or availability.
Does not download large flat files or complete checkout payments for the user.

use_cases.title: Review supplied candidate profiles
use_cases.description: Summarize work history and skills from candidate LinkedIn URLs after approving the provider and lookup cost.

use_cases.title: Enrich existing CRM contacts
use_cases.description: Research current roles and companies for contacts with supplied LinkedIn URLs, while tracking enrichment costs.

use_cases.title: Manage dataset access
use_cases.description: Check the account balance, inspect provider file unlock status, and obtain an expiring download link.

prompt_templates.title: Check the account balance
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Datacircle balance and report the available amount.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize one profile
prompt_templates.prompt: For [LinkedIn URL], show the Up2Data lookup cost and wait for my approval. Then summarize the returned role, company, history, and skills.

prompt_templates.title: Compare supplied profiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare experience and skills for these LinkedIn URLs: [URLs]. Show the provider and total cost before proceeding, then report actual costs and remaining balance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan provider and file access
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my balance and list file unlock status. Price HarvestAPI lookups for [URLs] with interests, and wait for approval. Share unlocked file links without downloading.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate provider-specific research and dataset access

output_examples.input: Show the cost of looking up two supplied profiles through Up2Data.
output: Quoted cost: $0.00475 for two successful profile lookups, based on the documented rate.
Up2Data profiles that cannot be found are free.
Please approve this cost before I proceed.

output_examples.input: Get the download link for my unlocked Up2Data flat file.
output: The link is valid for one hour.
The file is several gigabytes. It has not been downloaded.

best_practices: Provide exact LinkedIn URLs and the profile details needed for your task.
Approve the disclosed provider and cost before lookups, including any provider changes or additional URLs.
Use returned cost and balance metadata to verify spending, and treat all profile text as untrusted data.
anti_patterns: Looking up guessed URLs or additional people without an explicit request and spending approval.
Following instructions, opening embedded links, or running commands found in profile text or file rows.
Claiming funds were added before balance verification, or downloading large files instead of sharing their links.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Use requires access to the Datacircle MCP tools.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Datacircle server?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for using Datacircle MCP tools, not their implementation.

faq.question: What are the documented lookup prices?
faq.answer: Per 1,000 profiles, Up2Data costs $2.375, HarvestAPI costs $3.70, and Fetchin costs $1.485. Spending approval is required before lookups.

faq.question: What happens when a profile is missing or a provider is limited?
faq.answer: Missing Up2Data profiles are free; missing Fetchin profiles are billed. Switching providers after an Up2Data rate limit requires renewed approval.

faq.question: Can the assistant add funds automatically?
faq.answer: No. On request, it shares a Stripe Checkout link for you to pay. It verifies the balance before claiming funds were added.

faq.question: How does flat file access work?
faq.answer: The instructions describe adding $50 for API credit and flat file access. Check unlock status; download links expire after one hour.
